title: Teaching & Training
text:
I co-lead Open Climate Science for Agriculture, a NASA-funded curriculum that teaches researchers to use NASA satellite data and climate models for agricultural applications in a warming world. The materials are open, Python-based and available in English, French and Arabic.

title: Cereal Mapping and Area Estimation in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia
text:
Current
Winter cereals (durum wheat, bread wheat and barley) are the backbone of rainfed agriculture in the Maghreb. They are confined to a narrow belt between the Mediterranean and the Sahara. This project produces high-resolution maps of winter cereals across Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia, together with statistically rigorous, design-based estimates of cereal area. Both rest on field surveys carried out in all three countries.
Region: Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia · Collaborators: M. E. Brown, T. V. Loboda, S. Skakun, A. Endsley

title: Cereal Mapping and Area Estimation in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia
text:
Approach

Stratified sampling design. Primary sampling units are drawn by agricultural-density stratum. Field reference locations are visited within each unit.
Field campaigns. In 2023–2024, surveys recorded what was on the ground at each sampled location: cereal, fallow, tilled land, cereal under olive, olive, bare land and more.
Satellite classification. High-resolution Sentinel-2 imagery is classified for the 2023–2024 cropping season.
Design-based area estimation. Mapped and reference data are combined into unbiased cereal-area estimates with confidence intervals.




Sampling design: stratified sampling domain, a selected primary sampling unit, and a field reference observation.





Field photographs from the 2024 campaign paired with Sentinel-2 imagery, showing the agricultural states recorded on the ground.

title: Rain Rituals and Drought Governance
text:
Current Paper accepted
Rain prayer events (Salat al-Istisqa’) are a long-standing community and institutional response to drought across North Africa and the Middle East. This project asks whether calls for these prayers can serve as a ground-level signal of climate stress. It builds an event record from newspapers and news websites in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia (2000–2024) and compares it with the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) and conflict data. The aim is to understand how climate and conflict shocks interact in dryland societies.
Rituals were more likely as drought intensified, fell within the agricultural season, and tracked drought over rainfed cropland more closely than national averages. Together these results show that institutional recognition of drought follows where and when it hits farming. A related line of work looks at formal drought governance, including early-warning design in Algeria’s Drought Shield program.
Region: Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia · Collaborators: M. E. Brown, A. Endsley, W. Anderson, M. Enenkel, T. V. Loboda, G. Kaci

title: NASA HarvestStat
text:
Current
NASA HarvestStat is building the world’s most comprehensive global database of subnational crop production statistics. My work contributes data and quality control for North Africa. I also analyze how the region’s wheat systems have evolved, how volatile they are, and how sensitive they are to climate.
Region: global database; my analysis focuses on North Africa · Methods: compiling and quality-controlling subnational statistics, time-series and volatility analysis



Ripening wheat in eastern Algeria, June 2024. Wheat is the staple crop at the center of the North African analysis.

title: Drought and Agricultural Land-Use Change in North Africa
text:
Current
This research asks how drought shapes agricultural land use in the drylands of Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia: where cereals and other crops are grown, how cropland expands, contracts or intensifies, and how reliably this can be measured from space. It was the subject of my PhD dissertation, Drought and Agricultural Land-Use Change in North Africa (University of Maryland, 2026), and I am continuing it.
Region: Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia · Collaborators: M. E. Brown, T. V. Loboda

title: Drought and Agricultural Land-Use Change in North Africa
text:
Approach

High-resolution mapping of winter cereals from satellite imagery, trained and validated with field data collected for the project
Design-based estimates of cropland area built on probability sampling and field surveys
Long-term reconstruction of cropland area and yield, and comparison with agricultural statistics
Drought indices and satellite records of vegetation and soil moisture, linked to cropland dynamics

title: Welcome
text: Welcome to my website. I’ll use this blog for tutorials on remote sensing and climate data workflows, notes from workshops, and updates on my research on agriculture and drought in North Africa.

title: Walid Ouaret
text:
Walid Ouaret, Ph.D.
Postdoctoral Fellow · The Earth Commons Institute · Georgetown University

I study how climate extremes reshape agriculture, land use and critical infrastructure, and how people and institutions respond. I combine satellite observations, climate data and fieldwork to inform drought governance and resilience decisions.

I work with Roshanak (Roshi) Nateghi in the SuRGE Lab. Before Georgetown, I completed my PhD in Geographical Sciences at the University of Maryland (the story below).

title: Walid Ouaret
text:
The PhD story

I completed my PhD in Geographical Sciences at the University of Maryland in 2026, directed by Tatiana V. Loboda and mentored by Molly E. Brown. My dissertation, Drought and Agricultural Land-Use Change in North Africa, examined how drought shapes agricultural land use across Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia.
From the start, I wanted to put people in the equation. Satellites show where farmland changes, but not how societies experience drought. So alongside satellite and climate records, I read drought through the moment states publicly recognize it: state-organized rain rituals.
The work also meant going to the fields. Over the 2023–2024 season I drove thousands of kilometres through the cereal belt of all three countries, collecting an independent, probability-sampled ground truth to test how well satellite maps capture the region’s farmland.



1,350 field observations


3 countries surveyed


63 rain-ritual events recorded


25 yrs of cropland change analysed




01
People recognize drought where it hits farming. State-organized rain rituals (2000–2024) became more likely as drought intensified. All fell within the growing season, and drought over rainfed cropland predicted them better than national averages.
Accepted · Environmental Research: Climate


02
Fallow is where satellite maps disagree. Field-based estimates put cropland at 7.0 Mha in Morocco, 6.8 Mha in Algeria and 2.0 Mha in Tunisia. Fallow, nearly a third of all cropland, drives most of the disagreement among satellite products, and the cropland definition alone can flip the sign of the error.
In preparation for publication


03
When drought strikes matters most. Across 11,100 grid cells, persistent cropland change since 2000 occurred in 61% of analysed cells: expansion in Algeria, contraction in Morocco, both in Tunisia. Drought explained about half of that pattern, and seasonal timing was its strongest signal.
In preparation for publication



Why it matters. Better drought governance starts with what people experience on the ground. Early warning in drylands should track when and where drought strikes, not only how severe it is on average. It should pair satellite indicators with signals of how communities and institutions recognize drought, and it needs cropland maps built on consistent definitions and independent field data. The dissertation and its field dataset give agencies and researchers a practical basis for all three.

Research themes


Drought, Agriculture & Land-Use Change
Drought monitoring, cropland dynamics and satellite-based land-use assessment, validated with field surveys.


Drought Governance & Society

Emerging

Climate Risk & Infrastructure Resilience
Climate risks to energy and water systems, including drought-driven power-system vulnerability and the environmental footprint of data centers.



Earth Observation & Open Science

title: Agricultural and Environmental Modeling
section: Crop allocation in Tunisian rainfed smallholder systems
text:
Crop allocation in Tunisian rainfed smallholder systems
INRAE Landscape Modeling Team, Montpellier · 2018–2020 · IRD-ARTS grant (PI: Jean-Stéphane Bailly, AgroParisTech)
I collected data through farmer interviews and seasonal crop monitoring in the Lebna watershed using remote sensing. I combined these with expert elicitation to build and validate a crop allocation model for Tunisia’s rainfed smallholder farming systems.

title: Agricultural and Environmental Modeling
text:
Liming trade-offs in western Kenya
Plant Production Systems Group, Wageningen University · 2018
I built a database of field experiments on lime use in maize across Sub-Saharan Africa and ran a trade-off analysis linking yield effects to greenhouse gas emissions and farm income.

Hijbeek, R., van Loon, M. P., Ouaret, W., Boekelo, B., & van Ittersum, M. K. (2021). Liming agricultural soils in Western Kenya: Can long-term economic and environmental benefits pay off short term investments? Agricultural Systems, 190, 103095. doi:10.1016/j.agsy.2021.103095

title: Agricultural and Environmental Modeling

Organic and conventional yield synthesis
Global Agronomy Team, UMR Agronomie, INRAE, Paris · 2017
I compiled a global database comparing organic and conventional yields across crop species. I also designed a protocol to elicit quantitative expert knowledge on organic yields.

title: Agricultural and Environmental Modeling
text:
Urban expansion and peri-urban agriculture
Geospatial Analysis Center, Miami University · 2021–2023 · NASA Interdisciplinary Research in Earth Science (PI: Christopher Hain, NASA Marshall Space Flight Center)
As a graduate research assistant, I worked on the impact of urban expansion on peri-urban agriculture, hydrometeorology, food security and human health. I used GRACE, SMAP, MODIS, VIIRS, Planet, Sentinel, Landsat and other satellite data.

title: Mapping Agricultural Greenhouses in Algeria
text:
Current
Agricultural greenhouses are spreading quickly across Algeria, especially in the southern wilayas, but they are poorly documented. This project uses deep learning on satellite imagery to map them, and tracks how greenhouse agriculture has grown.

title: Research
text:
Current research



Current

Cereal Mapping and Area Estimation in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia
High-resolution winter cereal mapping and design-based area estimation across the North African cereal belt, built on field surveys in all three countries. Related work maps agricultural greenhouses in Algeria.

Region: Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia
Methods: stratified field sampling, Sentinel-2 classification, deep learning, design-based area estimation
Collaborators: M. E. Brown, T. V. Loboda, S. Skakun, A. Endsley, L. Shumilo
Status: ongoing; greenhouse mapping published (IEEE M2GARSS 2024)





Current

Drought and Agricultural Land-Use Change in North Africa
How drought shapes where and how cereals and other crops are grown, and how cropland expands, contracts or intensifies. This is the research line of my doctoral dissertation.

Region: Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia
Methods: satellite time series, drought indices, cropland mapping, agricultural statistics
Collaborators: M. E. Brown, T. V. Loboda
Status: ongoing; dissertation completed 2026





Current

Rain Rituals and Drought Governance
How communities and states recognize and respond to drought. Rain rituals and early-warning programs are read as signals of climate and conflict stress, to inform drought governance.

Region: North Africa and the Middle East
Methods: newspaper-archive event records, drought indices (SPEI), conflict data, statistical modeling
Collaborators: M. E. Brown, A. Endsley, W. Anderson, M. Enenkel, T. V. Loboda
Status: paper accepted in Environmental Research: Climate





Current

NASA HarvestStat
A global database of subnational crop production statistics. My work covers North Africa and the evolution, volatility and climate sensitivity of its wheat systems.

Region: global database; North Africa focus
Methods: compilation and quality control of subnational statistics, time-series analysis
Status: ongoing

title: SEEDS: Satellite-Enabled Earth Observation & Digital Solutions for Agriculture
text:
Role: Project Lead · Funding: 6th Grain · Period: 2025–2026
SEEDS puts satellite Earth observation and digital tools to work for agricultural decision-making. From October 14 to 17, 2025, the project ran the SEEDS Seminar Series: four days of talks on remote sensing and AI for agriculture and food security. It was held online and hosted by the Department of Geographical Sciences, University of Maryland. Speakers came from NASA Harvest, NASA Acres, Harvard and the University of Montana.
